items.summary: Crystal Palace FC or Oxbridge beckoned, but the multitalented MC kept forging her way towards music. She explains how she poured every aspect of herself into her debut mixtape Two weeks before we meet, UK rapper Cristale was scrambling down a cliff face to a secluded black pebbled beach in Dover, racing an incoming tide with fewer than 90 minutes to shoot the video for her single I’m Okay With Being Lonely. She’d never hiked before in her life. “I was wearing head-to-toe Stone Island, no hiking gear, full face of makeup, edges laid and Mum was doing my touch-ups on a rusty ladder,” she laughs.

items.title: Hiroshi Yoshimura :: Quiet Forest
items.summary: With no deceleration in sight, the 2020s have thus far been the decade of Kankyō Ongaku pioneer Hiroshi Yoshimura. 1996's Quiet Forest , the musician's final offering, is another gem in a slew of reissues courtesy of tireless label Temporal Drift. The Hoh Rainforest is the setting here, as Yoshimura interprets the terrain with his singular approach: superimposed synth soundscapes that contagiously mirror the greenery and precipitation: fluttering new age soundscapes as opulent as they are evocative. The post Hiroshi Yoshimura :: Quiet Forest first appeared on Aquarium Drunkard .

items.title: Ableton Live 13 hands-on: ARA 2, Drum Synth, new effects, more
items.summary: Ableton Live 13 is now in limited public beta. That includes a lot of what you've asked for, like multi-band Racks, overhauled preset navigation, and ARA 2 support for tools like Melodyne. And it's packed with new goodies: a very Ableton step sequencer, a multi-engine Drum Synth with some nice twists, new effects, a new ambient looper, and more. Also, I know some of you will like this: no mention of AI. It's like we just get to talk about music-making tools again. The post Ableton Live 13 hands-on: ARA 2, Drum Synth, new effects, more appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music .

items.title: Jon Hassell :: Music Is Invisible (Pentimento Volume Three)
items.summary: Music Is Invisible marks the third and final entry in Jon Hassell's Pentimento trilogy. Arriving five years after the experimental trumpeter's death, it's not exactly a studio album, but it's more than a live tape. As a record of a singular artist's psychic terroir, strong, mutable style and idiosyncratic sonic palette, it's a fittingly puzzling send-off. But rare elements of "straight Hassell" lurk in the mix, for those with the ears to see. The post Jon Hassell :: Music Is Invisible (Pentimento Volume Three) first appeared on Aquarium Drunkard .
